Jang Ho-Il

Introduction

015B (Gongil Obi) is widely recognized as Korea’s first producer group. Debuting in 1990, they have significantly influenced the Korean music landscape. The group was founded by Hyung-Gon Cho, Hyun-Chan Cho, and Seok-Won Jeong, former members of the band Caterpillar, who won the grand prize at the 1988 MBC University Song Festival.

The name 015B represents the concept of an “infinite orbit,” symbolizing endless creativity and musical exploration. It can also be read numerically as: nothing = 0, one = 1, and orbit = 5B, reflecting their philosophy of continual artistic evolution.

Over the course of their 35-year career, 015B has released a distinctive series of studio albums titled "Yearbooks(s)" which document their artistic growth and relevance in the industry. As of 2025, 015B continues to be active, regularly engaging with fans and releasing new music, sustaining their legacy as innovators in Korean music production. Their most notable albums include Yearbook 2018 (Released February 27, 2019) and Yearbook 2023 (Released February 28, 2024).

Besides their own music, 015B’s legacy includes their role as mentors and inspirations to many Korean hip-hop and R&B artists. Their pioneering production style and artistic integrity helped elevate the standards of Korean music production and opened doors for more experimental and genre-crossing projects.
